sentences.text: 1  ORDER 1.

By the present petition, the petitioners have impugned order dated 07.12.2024 of the Ld.
Magistrate whereby the three petitioners herein had been proceeded against by the Ld. Magistrate u/s 498A r/w section 34 IPC and they had been charged accordingly in case titled State Vs Govind Singh FIR No. 333/2023 PS Tilak Nagar.

entities.text: State Vs Govind Singh FIR No. 333/2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. By the present petition, the petitioners seek setting aside of the impugned order and their consequent discharge.

3. The primary argument of the petitioners is that there are no specific allegations of cruelty and/or harassment against the petitioners and despite this, the Ld. Magistrate has given a contrary finding.
The findings of the Ld. Magistrate as contained Crl. Revision no. 5/2025 Govind Singh & Ors Vs State & Anr 2/5 in the impugned order by which the petitioners are aggrieved is reproduced below:

entities.text: Crl. Revision no. 5/2025 Govind Singh & Ors Vs State & Anr 2/5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: " Perusal of complaint dated 07.07.2023 reveals that the complainant got married to the accused No.1, namely, Govind Singh, on 25.10.2021.
The complainant has alleged that her husband/accused no.1 and her father-in-law and mother-in-law i.e. accused no.2 and 3 used to inflict cruelty upon her and used to harass her by demanding dowry.
She has also submitted that certain demands of dowry were also fulfilled by her, however, despite that she was constantly subjected to the cruelty by the accused persons.
Prima facie, the complaint as well as chargsheet shows that there are specific allegations against all the accused persons to attract the offence u/s 498A/34 IPC qua all the accused persons".
4. The Ld. Counsel for the respondent has drawn attention of this Court to the statement of the complainant as recorded u/s 161 Cr.P.C, which contain the specific allegations.
5. There is no instance of cruelty/torture/harassment wherein the complainant alleges that the petitioners had used physical force upon her.
Hence, the nature of cruelty/torture/harassment complained of, is non-physical.
5.1. The allegations of cruelty cited by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent from the statement of the complainant recorded by the police are in the domain of 'mental cruelty'.
The instances cited relate to the general conduct of the petitioners and not beyond.
It is requirement of law that the allegations must be specific and by this it is meant that the allegations must go beyond generality of conduct and must be defined by their co- Crl.
Revision no. 5/2025 Govind Singh & Ors Vs State & Anr 3/5 ordinates of space and time.

entities.text: Govind Singh & Ors Vs State & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This because, if an event is not described by its time co-ordinate, the court will fail to ensure that it is conveyed to the accused/respondent/defendant/non-applicant that what he has to answer or defend in any proceeding against him.
In the present case, the instances of cruelty are not identified by their space-time co-ordinates.

Hence, they cannot be said to be specific whereas it is germane to criminal Govind Singh vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 21 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101169023/
2 proceedings that the allegations/accusations must be specific.
6.

entities.text: criminal Govind Singh vs State Of Nct Of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is admitted by both the parties that the complainant/respondent left the shared household on 21.08.2022 and the complaint to Authority was made on 02.03.2023.
It is also admitted fact that since 21.08.2022, the respondent/complainant is residing with her parents.

By these facts, it is manifest that the complainant/respondent had made the complaint which forms the foundation of the criminal case, not as a reaction to the alleged cruelty but as a meditated response, evident from prolonged time-lapse between the alleged wrong doings and its reporting.
7. It is admitted by both the parties that there is no documentary evidence to prove the grievance of the respondent/complainant.

By documentary evidence is meant text messages, call records, letters etc between the complainant/respondent and her benefactors such as her parents and/or friends,
wherein the complainant/respondent had cited specific incidents of torture.

8. Hence, it is found that the allegations are too general in nature and delayed so unreasonably that this delay leads to the Crl. Revision no. 5/2025 Govind Singh & Ors Vs State & Anr 4/5 inference that the complainant/respondent intended to use the process of law as a weapon against the petitioners and not as medicine for her redressal.

entities.text: Crl. Revision no. 5/2025 Govind Singh & Ors Vs State & Anr 4/5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In view of above discussions, the appeal stands allowed.
Accordingly, the impugned order dated 07.12.2024 is set aside.
The petitioners- Gobind Singh, Ravinder Singh and Amrit Kaur are discharged.
10. TCR along with attested copy of this order be sent to the Ld. Trial Court.
11. The revision petition file be consigned to record room.
